title: Spatial cotensors and categorical homotopy equivalences
statement: Let $\mathcal V$ be presentably monoidal, and use [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Write $U(C)$ for the object space of an algebroid $C$, and $\mathcal S$ for spaces with cartesian tensor. Let $B,C\in\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$ and $H,K\in\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal S)$. For a finite set $S$ and $\mathcal W\in\{\mathcal V,\mathcal S\}$, let $E_S^{\mathcal W}$ denote the indiscrete $\mathcal W$-algebroid with object space $S$ and all mapping objects the tensor unit, with unit constraints as composition and units. There is an action $B\diamond K$ of $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal S)$ on $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$: its objects are pairs, and its mapping objects are $K(k,k')\odot B(b,b')$, where $T\odot v=\operatorname{colim}_{T}v$ is the copower by a space. This action has right cotensors $C^K$, with natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(B\diamond K,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B,C^K)$. For the indiscrete space-enriched algebroids $E^n_{\mathcal S}$ on $n+1$ objects, one has $B\diamond E^0_{\mathcal S}\simeq B$, $E^p_{\mathcal V}\diamond E^q_{\mathcal S}\simeq E^{(p+1)(q+1)-1}_{\mathcal V}$, $C^{E^0_{\mathcal S}}\simeq C$, and $U(C^{E^n_{\mathcal S}})\simeq\operatorname{Map}(E^n_{\mathcal V},C)$; also $(C^K)^H\simeq C^{H\times K}$ naturally, where $H\times K$ is the cartesian product of space-enriched algebroids. A natural equivalence between $F,G:B\to C$ means a map $B\diamond E^1_{\mathcal S}\to C$ with endpoints $F,G$. A categorical equivalence $F:B\to C$ means a functor $G:C\to B$ and natural equivalences $GF\simeq 1_B$ and $FG\simeq1_C$. Every categorical equivalence is fully faithful and essentially surjective. For every complete $Z$, a categorical equivalence $F:B\to C$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(C,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(B,Z)$. For any map of nonempty finite sets $f:S\to T$, the map $E_f:E_S^{\mathcal W}\to E_T^{\mathcal W}$ is a categorical equivalence for $\mathcal W=\mathcal V$ or $\mathcal S$. Cotensoring contravariantly with a categorical equivalence of space-enriched algebroids gives a categorical equivalence of $\mathcal V$-algebroids.

source.place: Corollary 4.3.17, Definition 4.3.18, Proposition 5.1.11 and Lemma 5.1.12, Definition 5.5.1 and Definition 5.5.2, Proposition 5.5.3, Corollary 5.5.6 (restricted to nonempty finite sets), Lemma 5.5.7, Theorem 5.5.13 (read online; not archived in literature/). No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Put $b(T,v)=T\odot v=\operatorname{colim}_{T}v$. Distributing tensor over the two colimits gives $(T\odot v)\otimes(T'\odot v')\simeq(T\times T')\odot(v\otimes v')$, with the singleton giving the unit. These comparisons define a strong monoidal functor $b:\mathcal S\times\mathcal V\to\mathcal V$: for any finite list, the comparison is the universal colimit cocone indexed by the product of its spaces, so regrouping or inserting a singleton gives the same cocone and all coherences. The same universal property gives $(T\times T')\odot v\simeq T\odot(T'\odot v)$. Apply the external-product statement to $K\boxtimes B$ and change enrichment by $b$. This constructs $B\diamond K$ with the claimed object pairs and mapping objects, including its coherent compositions and units. The preceding Fubini comparisons, natural in the operadic diagrams, give the action equivalences $(B\diamond H)\diamond K\simeq B\diamond(H\times K)$ and the unit $B\diamond E^0_{\mathcal S}\simeq B$. In spaces this action is the cartesian product of space-enriched algebroids. No symmetry on $\mathcal V$ is used: the order of the $v$ factors is retained.

source.place: Corollary 4.3.17 and its spatial action; explicit copower construction

proof.text: The copower functor $b$ preserves colimits separately. In $v$ this follows by interchanging colimits; in $T$ the copower universal property is $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(T\odot v,w)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(T,\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,w))$, so colimits of spaces become limits on mapping out. The bilinear-colimit statement therefore applies to $b$ and the external product from step 1. Thus $-\diamond K$ preserves small colimits. The algebroid category is presentable by the presentability statement, so the presentable adjoint criterion gives its right adjoint $C^K$ with $\operatorname{Map}(B\diamond K,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B,C^K)$. Naturality in $K$ gives the contravariant cotensor maps. Applying this adjunction twice gives $\operatorname{Map}(B,(C^K)^H)\simeq\operatorname{Map}((B\diamond H)\diamond K,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B,C^{H\times K})$. Yoneda identifies the represented objects and gives the natural iterated-cotensor equivalence. Because these are equivalences of coherent mapping-space bifunctors, the units, counits and composition compatibilities are those of the adjunctions, rather than choices of objectwise bijections.

All hom spaces of $E^q_{\mathcal S}$ are singletons, whose copowers are the original objects. Thus $E^p_{\mathcal V}\diamond E^q_{\mathcal S}$ has $(p+1)(q+1)$ objects and every hom object and composition is the unit and its constraints, giving the stated indiscrete formula. The unit action and adjunction give $C^{E^0_{\mathcal S}}\simeq C$. The equivalence-nerve statement identifies $U(A)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(E^0_{\mathcal V},A)$ for any algebroid $A$; hence $U(C^{E^n_{\mathcal S}})\simeq\operatorname{Map}(E^0_{\mathcal V}\diamond E^n_{\mathcal S},C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(E^n_{\mathcal V},C)$. These identifications commute with maps of finite sets because their hom maps are identities of the tensor unit.

source.place: Definitions 5.1.4 and 5.5.1; finite indiscrete action formulas

proof.text: Use the displayed cylinder maps as the definitions of natural equivalence and categorical equivalence. Let $F:B\to C$ have pseudo-inverse $G$ with witnesses $GF\Rightarrow1_B$ and $FG\Rightarrow1_C$. Restriction of the second witness to an object $c$ gives an equivalence $FGc\to c$, so the equivalence-nerve criterion makes $F$ essentially surjective. To check full faithfulness fix $x,y\in U(B)$ and write $\alpha:B(x,y)\to C(Fx,Fy)$, $\gamma:C(Fx,Fy)\to B(GFx,GFy)$ and $\delta:B(GFx,GFy)\to C(FGFx,FGFy)$ for the maps induced by $F,G,F$. Naturality of the first witness says that $\gamma\alpha$ is conjugation by its components at $x,y$; it is an equivalence because composition with an equivalence of objects induces equivalences of hom objects. Naturality of the second witness at $Fx,Fy$ says that $\delta\gamma$ is likewise an equivalence. In the homotopy category of $\mathcal V$, $\alpha(\gamma\alpha)^{-1}$ is a right inverse of $\gamma$, and $(\delta\gamma)^{-1}\delta$ is a left inverse. A left and right inverse coincide, so $\gamma$ and then $\alpha$ are invertible. Thus $\alpha$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal V$ for every pair, which is full faithfulness. The conjugation identities follow by restricting the cylinder functor to the two objects and their hom object and using its compatibility with composition.

For $f:S\to T$ with $S,T$ nonempty finite, choose $s_0\in S$ and let $g:T\to S$ be constant with value $s_0$. Define $h_S:S\times\{0,1\}\to S$ by $h_S(s,0)=gf(s)$, $h_S(s,1)=s$, and $h_T:T\times\{0,1\}\to T$ by $h_T(t,0)=fg(t)$, $h_T(t,1)=t$. Step 3 identifies $E_S^{\mathcal W}\diamond E^1_{\mathcal S}$ with $E_{S\times\{0,1\}}^{\mathcal W}$, and likewise for $T$. Send every hom object by the identity $\mathbf1\to\mathbf1$ and every object by $h_S$ or $h_T$. Unit constraints make these algebroid functors, with endpoints $E_gE_f,1$ and $E_fE_g,1$. They are the required natural equivalences, so $E_g$ is a pseudo-inverse of $E_f$ for both enrichments. This uses identity hom maps, not a claim that the tensor unit of $\mathcal V$ is terminal.

Let $u:K\to H$ have pseudo-inverse $v:H\to K$. Contravariance gives $C^u:C^H\to C^K$ and $C^v:C^K\to C^H$. For the witness $w_K:K\times E^1_{\mathcal S}\to K$ from $vu$ to $1_K$, apply cotensor contravariance to obtain $C^{w_K}:C^K\to C^{K\times E^1_{\mathcal S}}\simeq(C^K)^{E^1_{\mathcal S}}$. Its adjunct is a map $C^K\diamond E^1_{\mathcal S}\to C^K$. Its endpoints are $C^{vu}=C^uC^v$ and $1_{C^K}$, by naturality of the adjunction from step 2. The witness $w_H:H\times E^1_{\mathcal S}\to H$ gives by the explicitly identical construction $C^H\xrightarrow{C^{w_H}}C^{H\times E^1_{\mathcal S}}\simeq(C^H)^{E^1_{\mathcal S}}$, whose adjunct has endpoints $C^vC^u$ and $1_{C^H}$. These are the two natural-equivalence witnesses, proving the final cotensor assertion.

We now justify the use of completeness in the remaining mapping-space assertion, without using the completion theorem, which depends on this item. Write $I_n(Z)=\operatorname{Map}(E^n_{\mathcal V},Z)$ and $Q=|I_\bullet(Z)|$. By the equivalence-nerve statement this is a groupoid object. Effectiveness of groupoid objects gives $I_n(Z)\simeq U(Z)\times_Q\cdots\times_QU(Z)$. For complete $Z$, $U(Z)\to Q$ is an equivalence, so every augmentation $I_n(Z)\to Q$ is an equivalence, compatibly with all simplicial maps. Put $A=Z^{E^1_{\mathcal S}}$. The adjunction and finite formula identify $I_n(A)\simeq I_{2n+1}(Z)$, where the $2n+2$ objects are ordered as $(0,0),\ldots,(0,n),(1,0),\ldots,(1,n)$ in coordinates $(e,i)$ (the two factors have been interchanged). Every simplicial operator is induced by $(e,i)\mapsto(e,\theta(i))$, which is monotone even when $\theta$ is not injective; hence these identifications give a simplicial augmentation $I_\bullet(A)\to Q$ that is an equivalence in every degree. Its realization is $Q$ (the simplex indexing category has contractible nerve, since $[0]$ is initial in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$). Thus $U(A)=I_0(A)\to|I_\bullet(A)|$ is an equivalence, proving $A$ complete. By steps 5-6 the map $j=Z^s:Z\simeq Z^{E^0_{\mathcal S}}\to A$, for $s:E^1_{\mathcal S}\to E^0_{\mathcal S}$, is a categorical equivalence. Step 4 makes it fully faithful and essentially surjective; the nerve criterion gives $I(j)$ an equivalence, and completeness of both ends then gives $U(j)$ an equivalence. The last criterion in the nerve statement now makes $j$ an equivalence of algebroids.

source.place: Lemmas 5.4.8 and 5.5.8; effectiveness calculation replacing the locality argument

proof.text: For any $D$, set $P_D=\operatorname{Map}(D,Z)$ and $R_D=\operatorname{Map}(D\diamond E^1_{\mathcal S},Z)$. Adjunction identifies the map $q_D:P_D\to R_D$ induced by $s$ with $\operatorname{Map}(D,j)$, so step 7 makes $q_D$ an equivalence. The two endpoint restrictions $r_0,r_1:R_D\to P_D$ satisfy $r_iq_D\simeq1$ because $sd^i=1$; therefore both are inverses of $q_D$, giving $r_0\simeq r_1$ naturally in $D$. Given $F:B\to C$ with inverse $G$ and witnesses $w_B,w_C$, postcomposition of $w_B:B\diamond E^1_{\mathcal S}\to B$ by a variable map $B\to Z$ gives a map $P_B\to R_B$ whose endpoints are precomposition by $GF$ and the identity. The homotopy $r_0\simeq r_1$ makes those two endomorphisms of $P_B$ homotopic. Postcomposing $w_C$ by maps $C\to Z$ gives, with the same endpoint calculation on $P_C\to R_C$, a homotopy from precomposition by $FG$ to the identity on $P_C$. Thus $F^*:P_C\to P_B$ and $G^*:P_B\to P_C$ are homotopy inverses, proving the mapping-space assertion for every complete $Z$.
